title: PR Heuristics & Post-merge Triggers — Scratchpad
body:
Context:
This is a lightweight personal scratchpad for fast, repeatable PR review decisions and follow-ups. I keep coming back to the same heuristics during busy sprints — putting them here so I can (a) move quicker when triaging reviews and (b) create automation tickets for the things we keep re-checking manually.

High-level goals for any PR I review quickly:
- Safety: no obvious data leakage, secrets, or credential changes.
- Correctness & tests: behavioral changes covered by tests or accompanied by a short manual verification plan.
- Observability: add metrics/logs/traces for important state changes or error conditions introduced.
- Performance cost: any change that affects serving path must be considered for p99 and token cost.
- Simplicity: prefer smaller, incremental changes over large, sweeping refactors unless justified.

Quick triage checklist (first 60–120s) — decide depth of review:
1) Files changed > 300 lines? -> Deep review required. Large diffs hide risk.
2) Any changes in: routing layer, caching, kv cache, kernel selection, batching? -> Deep review & SRE consult.
3) Tests added/modified? If none and behavior changes -> request tests or a runbook.
4) CI failures? If flaky CI or unrelated failures -> rerun, but do not merge unless green on the relevant job(s).
5) New prod dependencies or native libs? -> security + infra review.
6) Secrets/KMS/HSM usage changes? -> block and escalate to security.
7) Docs/console/SDK surface area change? -> product review.

Concrete heuristics by difftype:
- Config-only changes (feature flags, timeouts): Verify rollout knob, default behavior, and docs. Prefer canary rollout.
- Experiment toggles (A/B): confirm experiment metric and kill switch exist.
- Model change (model id, quantization profile): locate benchmark results or ask for recent perf numbers (latency, memory, token cost).
- Query path changes: ensure we either keep existing SLOs or add compensating optimizations (batching, caching).

Suggested review checklist (what I typically add as comments):
- "Add unit/integration test to cover X" or "Please add a small e2e with fixture Y"
- "Why was approach A (existing) dropped in favor of B? Can we keep backwards compatibility?"
- "Add a metric for failed path Z (counter + sample log)"
- "This function is on hot path — add microbenchmark or include complexity note"
- "This change will affect billing: confirm with product or mention in release notes"

Follow-ups / tickets I routinely create after merging quick fixes:
- LINT: Add rule to catch use of raw SQL string formatting in repo (ENG-xxxx).
- CI: Add job that runs minimal perf check on PR if it touches serving runtime (ENG-xxxx).
- MONITORING: Auto-create dashboard panel when new route is added (instrumentation checklist).
- SRE: Add a trace sampling marker for the new handler function.

Automation ideas (low friction):
- PR size bot: warn at >250 LOC changed with a short checklist template.
- Serving-path labeler: auto-label PRs that touch known serving directories (serving-runtime/, kernels/, batching/). Labels trigger different reviewers.
- Quick perf smoke: Collector job that runs a simple 1s generation locally in CI container for PRs touching models/serving code. Fail on >20% p50 regression vs baseline. (start with warning mode)

Notes to self: common blindspots I've missed before
- Hidden config: environment variables read by process but not declared in config schema — add to docs and DRY.
- Cache invalidation subtlety when changing key format — always search for storage consumers across services.
- Local dev only: tests passing locally but CI container differs (GPU vs CPU); ensure test matrix covers both where relevant.

Post-merge quick checklist (first 24h):
- Confirm CI deployments passed and smoke tests executed.
- Watch deployment for 1–2 canary cycles (or equivalent traffic window) for regressions at p99 latency.
- If change touched model selection/routing, validate sample requests and end-to-end traces.
- If any alerts fire, rollback or initiate quick postmortem.

Personal TODOs (action items I want to file from this doc)
- [ ] File ENG ticket: "PR size bot + serving-path labeler" — description + basic design (blocking: infra support for labeler).
- [ ] Add lightweight perf-check job in our PR CI: prototype as a GitHub Action.
- [ ] Draft small doc for "How to review serving-runtime PRs" for new eng hires (one-pager).
- [ ] Add lint rule for string-based SQL & templated blob writes.

Rough example comment templates (copy-paste friendly):
- "Thanks! Quick note: this touches the serving path. Can you add a microbenchmark or explain why p99 latency won't be impacted? If possible run the perf-smoke CI job locally and paste results."
- "Heads-up: please add a unit test or a short manual verification plan for error case X. Without it we're likely to regress silently."
- "Flagging for SRE/security: this PR changes credentials handling — please hold merge until review."

Random notes / brain dump (freeform):
- We over-index on test counts but not on meaningful smoke tests for production paths. Maybe a PR checklist that requires a single "happy path smoke" for serving changes would reduce regressions.
- For small UX/console changes, short manual QA steps in the PR description saved me time in the past.

End — will re-iterate this into a proper internal doc if I keep repeating these comments.

Signed: Priya
